description: Participants build vision systems for a fictional municipal roads and traffic department that must keep working in glare, dust, rain and at night. On public road-damage images and synthetic traffic-camera clips they audit and extend annotations, fine-tune convolutional and transformer backbones, train a pothole detector and a crack segmenter, track and count vehicles, and fit the chosen model to the latency and memory budget of a processor-only roadside unit. Each lab ends with a test under changed lighting, blur or camera position. Vision-language models and multimodal applications are AE-408.
audience: Practitioners. Engineers who have completed the level 200 set or can show equivalent work: a deployed model or language model application they built and can explain.
prerequisites: AE-201 Machine Learning Foundations and Model Evaluation
AE-202 Deep Learning and Generative AI Fundamentals
Trains a neural network with a hand-written training loop
Computes precision and recall from a confusion matrix

outcomes.text: Prepare an image dataset with annotation guidelines, an agreement check, splits that keep each road segment in one split, and augmentations that preserve label meaning, given road images with partial labels and near-duplicate frames
outcomes.evidence: a dataset card, an agreement score and a split report with no road segment shared across splits

outcomes.text: Implement transfer learning with two pretrained backbones and compare them by condition slice with intervals, given defect crops and a free notebook GPU
outcomes.evidence: a comparison table by lighting and weather slice with bootstrap intervals

outcomes.text: Build a detector and a segmenter and diagnose their errors by type to choose the next improvement, given pothole boxes and crack masks
outcomes.evidence: average precision and overlap metrics, an error breakdown and a justified next step

outcomes.text: Measure tracking and counting accuracy for vehicles crossing a line in video, given synthetic camera clips with ground-truth counts
outcomes.evidence: count error per clip and the number of identity switches

outcomes.text: Optimise a model to a per-frame latency and memory budget on a processor through export, input resolution and quantisation, re-measuring accuracy at each step, given the roadside unit's stated budget
outcomes.evidence: a benchmark table and the chosen operating point

outcomes.text: Evaluate the model under corruption and camera shift and decide whether to release it, given rain, glare, night and moved-camera test sets
outcomes.evidence: a model card with results per condition, privacy controls and a release decision defended live
